causalHypothesis.statement: The finale token is cancelled by the normal handback itself, one rendered frame after it. StoryDirectorDriver.tsx:145 computes foreground with story.active as a conjunct, so the moment completeChapter13/completeStory sets active:false the very next frame takes the !foreground branch and calls suspendCommonGroundPresentation('visibility-loss') (or 'pause'), which cancels the live token unconditionally — even though the document is visible, the app is playing and nothing was paused.
causalHypothesis.confidence: high for the source route; the specific firing caller is INFERRED, not observed
supportingFit: Quantitative fit: 0.0235 s ≈ 1.4 frames at 60 Hz — exactly the 'survived the handback frame, died on the next one' shape, not a 5 s deadline and not an instantaneous same-frame kill.
Every other clear route is excluded (E4, E5, no caller for releaseCommonGroundChapter) or requires an audio-block state that E3 shows was false ~24 ms earlier.

It explains why the two deliberate retention mechanisms (storyDirector.ts:1232 exception, commonGroundDirector.ts:653 done-frame deadline carrier, documented at StoryDirectorDriver.tsx:223-226) are effectively unreachable in normal play: an earlier-priority frame callback cancels first.
causalHypothesis.contractRelation: If confirmed, this is a clear attributable SOLELY to ordinary handback/done with no declared cancellation, which is exactly the case the score interpretation and producer review call conflicting with the explicit retention exception. Nothing here asserts an audible failure, an audible minimum, a fixed 5 s performance, or that anyone heard anything.
notClaimed: No audible onset, silence, loudness, mix or release-envelope claim.
The reason label passed to cancelCommonGroundFinalTexture is discarded (parameter is `_reason`, commonGroundScore.ts:259), so no runtime evidence of WHICH reason fired exists in any current capture.
No repair, patch, replacement implementation or acceptance is proposed.

measurementPlan.goal: Distinguish 'cancelled by story-inactive foreground check' from 'cancelled by audio-block' and from 'paused', and measure exact token lifetime in frames — using ONLY existing read-only hooks, no source/probe/contract change.

smallestExecutableStep.lane: the existing arrival-common journey probe, movie lane, same URL/preview identity
smallestExecutableStep.window: from 2 s before the ch13 commit to 8 s after (covers begin, any cancel, and the 5 s deadline + 4.5 s release if it ever survives)
smallestExecutableStep.method: ONE page.evaluate per poll at ~4-8 ms containing ALL of the following reads so the record is atomic (this is the fix for E1 — no new hook is needed, only co-location):
readsPerPoll: window.__voxBundleDiag()  (score bundle trace + heldChain: whether the override was actually held/released)
derived: t_begin = first poll with finalTextureSeconds !== null, minus its own age
t_clear = first poll with finalTextureSeconds === null after t_begin
t_inactive = first poll with story.active === false
lifetimeMs = t_clear - t_begin, and (t_clear - t_inactive) in ms and in estimated frames

decisionRule: If (t_clear - t_inactive) is within ~1-2 frames AND visibilityState==='visible' AND hasFocus() AND __voxAudioDiag shows a live running route across the window => the clear is caused by the story-inactive foreground branch (StoryDirectorDriver.tsx:145-151). That is a cancellation attributable solely to normal handback/done.

If __voxAudioDiag / context state shows the route not running or music muted at or before t_clear => the audio-block cancel (commonGroundDirector.ts:576-579) is the responsible path, which IS a declared cancellation and explains the early clear without any audible-minimum claim.
If t_clear precedes t_inactive => neither; re-open the enumeration.
In every branch, record __voxBundleDiag heldChain across t_clear so the existing 4.5 s release is observed as state, separately from any audible claim.
